title: Peace Talks in Kyiv: US Envoys Meet Zelensky
summary:
Have you ever tried to get two friends who are fighting to make up? That's kind of what's happening between Ukraine and Russia. But it's a really big deal because it's a war, and lots of people are hurt.

This week, two important Americans went to Ukraine to talk to President Volodymyr Zelensky. Their names are Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. They work for President Donald Trump. They also went to Russia to talk to President Vladimir Putin. That's a lot of traveling!

They are trying to help stop the war. Zelensky said Ukraine is ready to talk about ending the war, but he wants "security guarantees" (promises that Ukraine will be safe) and a "dignified" peace (a fair and respectful end).

One cool thing: Putin and Zelensky agreed to stop attacking each other's capitals for three days while the envoys were visiting. That means no bombs on Kyiv or Moscow for a little while. That's like a time-out in a game.

The envoys said they felt "encouraged" after the talks. Kushner said Trump wants to find a way to end the war and make a peace that lasts a long time.

But it's not easy. Even during the talks, there were more attacks. Ukraine said Russia sent 108 drones and small missiles overnight. Ukraine's air defenses shot down 82 drones and six missiles, but 11 places were hit.

Zelensky wrote on social media that Ukraine has always been "constructive" (trying to help) and wants peace. He said, "Peace is needed. Security guarantees are needed."

So, will there be peace? It's too early to say. But at least they are talking. And that's a start.
why_it_matters: When countries fight, talking can be a first step to fixing the problem — just like talking through an argument with a friend can keep things from getting worse.
